newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher with London closed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher with London closed.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly higher Monday, on moderate volumes, while London and Hong Kong markets were closed for holidays.

"We saw some trade and fund buying on a day in which it was probably easier to make the high print with London and Hong Kong out, but there was some good quality fund buying seen," North American Equity Services floor trader John Geraghty said.
COMEX December gold ended up $1.30 an ounce at $394.50, after seeing a two week high at $394.60 intraday on total estimated volume in the gold strip of 11,000 lots.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted late at $389.20/389.70, from a London afternoon fix Friday of $387.50, and a New York close Friday at $388.00/388.50.
Meanwhile world gold mine production is seen increasing steadily over the next three years, reaching 83.1 million ounces by 1998, the Washington DC based Gold Institute said.
COMEX December silver, now the active contract with more open interest, ended up 5.6 cents at $5.330 an ounce after seeing a high of $5.355, its highest level since early June.
Both gold and silver have been recovering since early July from a downtrend since February this year.
The focus this week is likely to be on the first notice day Friday for August gold and silver and on the roll from September to December in silver, traders said.
September silver is approaching its delivery period, beginning September 2, but December silver is now the active month with more open interest.

"Fund buying of silver on the back of technical recommendations has opened up the possibility that silver will soon break through the $5.30-5.40 level basis spot," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.
"We would expect to see good forward selling from producers and smelters at those levels and higher," he said.
NYMEX October platinum ended up $2.10 an ounce at $405.50, while NYMEX December palladium, now the active contract, ended down $0.45 at $126.75.

While platinum prices have been recovering along with gold and silver in the past two months, palladium has remained weak, sinking to two and a half year lows last week, on news of new catalyst technology developed by General Motors, which some traders interpreted as lowering demand for palladium.
"There are some tentative signs the Russians have taken fright and eased up on their sales to the West in an effort to stabilize the palladium price," Arnold said in a weekly report.
"The worst of the downside is probably over now but we would be surprised to see palladium prices moving much above the $135-$140 level basis spot in the next few months."
